Ligand 1 again. One of my clearest negative results was benzothiazol-2-ylamino scoring 0.01 where pyrimidin-2-ylamino scored 0.10, but that fragment changed two things at once: it fused a benzo ring on, and it introduced sulfur. I read it as the fusion, consistent with quinazoline also failing, but I have not actually separated the two. A monocyclic 2-aminothiazole settles it: sulfur present, fusion absent, and the ring nitrogen still ortho to the bridging NH. Atom 6 is the aromatic carbon bearing the arylamine at atom 7 over a non-ring bond, so I cut it and attach thiazol-2-ylamino. If this scores like the pyridine and pyrimidine links, fusion is the disqualifier and I can keep using sulfur heterocycles; if it scores like the benzothiazole, sulfur is the problem. It is also a reasonable molecule - the thiazole is two atoms lighter than a pyrimidine, so MW drops.
